text:
@WingardT Thanks for getting back to me on that.

I feel its too expensive these days, especially when it comes to PC gaming and keeping up with the hardware.

Back when I was PC gaming in the 2000s (mainly from 2000 to around 2007), I was always able to run most new releases on max settings. But as we approached 2007 (the year I stopped), I found myself losing interest in upgrading my rig to play the latest AAA titles. I remember looking at the original Chernobyl game and reading the system requirements on the back of the box. I thought, 'This won’t even run on medium settings on my rig...hah!' I ended up putting it back on the shelf in some game store.

I did, however, join the new-gen console market a bit late. In 2011, I bought a brand new PS3 (I had a new job, so I could afford it), and it came bundled with Uncharted or something – a fantastic game, I must say. I ended up playing most of them, along with the Resistance series, FNC, Dead Island, Batman: Arkham Asylum and Arkham City, The Last of Us (one of the greatest video gaming experiences of all time, what an emotional roller coaster that was wow..), and GTA V. I eventually sold it in early 2016, but the PS3 was, without a doubt, the best console gaming experience I’ve ever had, especially during my early-to-mid 30s!

PC gaming in the 2000s was the pinnacle for me, even if I missed out on the final few years of that decade. 2003–2004 was truly the 'sweet spot' in terms of nostalgia. ☺
